key_insight: vid2vid-long uses explicit correspondences across video frames to support long-range temporal consistency. The central idea is to connect relevant content across time rather than rely only on a short window of recent frames.
problem_solved: Fast video-to-video methods restrict attention to a fixed-length causal window, making it difficult to preserve consistency when relevant earlier frames fall outside that window.
method: Introduce a correspondence-based approach called vid2vid-long.
Use explicit cross-frame relationships available in video-to-video translation to connect matching content over time.
Address the limitations of short temporal context for interactive video generation.
impact: The approach targets interactive video editing and translation that need both responsiveness and stable appearance over time. The provided abstract is truncated, so implementation details and measured performance cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Timeline showing relevant historical frames falling outside a fixed attention window.
Frame-to-frame diagram with matching objects connected by correspondence lines.
Conceptual comparison: short-window generation versus correspondence-guided consistency.
Paired stopwatch and linked-frame icons representing speed and temporal stability.
paper_title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
paper_authors: Gaurav Parmar, Zhengqi Li, Richard Zhang, Jun-Yan Zhu, Srinivasa Narasimhan
